title: Campaign-led traffic escrow for safe rollouts and replayable auto-rollback
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a traffic escrow subsystem and accompanying client SDK primitives to coordinate safe canary/A-B/shadow exposures. The escrow acts as a short-lived immutable ledger of candidate requests and routing decisions so exposures can be replayed, audited, or force-rolled back deterministically. Deliverables: control-plane REST/gRPC endpoints, a lightweight escrow client helper, idempotency token scheme, RBAC scopes for escrow operations, and a migration shim for existing traffic-manifests.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane exposes /escrow/submit, /escrow/confirm, /escrow/replay REST endpoints and equivalent gRPC methods.
SDK provides a rolloutEscrow client with helpers: openCampaign(), submitBatch(items), confirmExposure(batch_id), requestReplay(batch_id,timestamp).
Each escrowed batch is immutable and associated with an idempotency token and campaign metadata for auditability.
Auto-rollback policy can subscribe to escrow delta metrics and trigger deterministic replay-based rollback when configured thresholds are breached.
RBAC scopes rollout.escrow.write, rollout.escrow.replay, rollout.escrow.admin are enforced and audited in the control plane.
Integration tests covering REST and gRPC paths, and an end-to-end canary that demonstrates a replay-triggered rollback in staging.
Performance regression <5% p95 tail latency for high QPS workloads when escrow is enabled in the critical path (with batching and async confirm flows documented).
technical_notes: Escrow design: short-lived append-only ledger stored in dedicated control-plane table with TTL and materialized metrics export.
Idempotency: campaign-scoped UUIDv4 token + monotonic sequence per client. Server rejects duplicate batch_id for same campaign with 409 response and returns existing batch metadata.

Confirm vs async confirm: clients may use optimistic async confirm to reduce latency (submit returns provisional acceptance) and later confirm to finalize exposure. Control plane supports provisional->final transitions.

Replay: replay endpoint accepts batch_id and target variant to replay requests against the promoted model; replay runs through sandboxed path to compute impact metric deltas without counting against production quotas unless explicitly approved.

Metrics/rollback predicates: support registering a policy using metric id, window, comparator, and threshold (e.g., latency_p95 > 250ms for 5m). Policy engine evaluates against escrowed exposures and can trigger replay or automatic rollback actions.
RBAC: map scopes to tokens and service principals. Ensure private/dedicated customers can map to their KMS-backed service identity.
Backward compatibility: provide migration adapter that converts existing traffic-manifests into ephemeral escrow campaigns for a configurable period before full migration.
Telemetry: escrow events emit structured traces and audit logs with batch_id, campaign, submitter, and decision timestamps for tracing incidents.
Storage: use append-only sharded table with per-campaign GC. Consider S3 offload for cold storage of large payloads with pointers in the ledger.
Security: escrow payloads may contain redacted request contexts. Provide encryption-at-rest and KMS integration for on-prem and private deployments.
